## 8922fefc96ff

**Reproduced teaching/support defect; audit target left unchanged.** Current
generator version `2.0.1` has SHA-256
`39ac60c259165d082dfa437086cdd60af9a61ac3089c86e38f6bc23009da8187`.
It does not declare `RULE_HASH`; canonical `apply` executes rule hash
`fcbcb48853c9` and confirms catalog agreement.

### Finding A2 — empty-interior precondition can disappear from the demonstrations

The intended row rule fills between two orange endpoints only when every interior
cell is black. A plausible shortcut is: **fill every row containing exactly two
orange cells, without checking the interior**. Ordinary easy and medium draws
never emit an occupied interior, so this rival is observationally equivalent on
those bands. Hard draws sometimes emit a blocker, but there is no lesson hook or
schedule that guarantees the branch appears in the demonstrations.

A normal no-override hard lesson reproduces the defect:
`seed=22`, sample indices `0..4`, four demonstrations and one query. All four
demonstrations have clear endpoint spans, so the rival matches **4/4** canonical
outputs. The query has orange endpoints at columns 6 and 10 of row 5 with interior
`[2,0,0]`; canonical Racket leaves that row unchanged, while the rival overwrites
three cells. The input passes the current `self_check`.

A fresh finite diagnostic census used seeds `0..299` in each band and five pair
draws per lesson: **900 lessons / 4,500 pair draws**. Easy and medium produced
0/1,500 occupied-span pairs each and the rival survived all 300 lessons in each
band. Hard produced 629/1,500 occupied-span pairs; the rival survived all four
demonstrations in 26/300 hard lessons and failed 14 subsequent queries. Overall it
survived 626/900 demonstration sets and failed 14/900 queries. The declared
`texture="span_already_filled"` is also an accepted counterexample, but the
retained seed-22 witness is ordinary production output.

Evidence and reproducer:

- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/episode.jsonl`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/input.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/rival-output.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/report.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/probe.py`

Recommended repair: make occupied-span rows ordinary across bands or guarantee at
least one such Racket-labelled demonstration whenever the query may contain one;
add the unconditional-two-endpoint rival to a semantic lesson contract. A prior
unverified review-index claim was used only as a lead—the current source, exact
lesson, census, validator result, and Racket output were independently reproduced.

## 8922fefc96ff

**Classification: reproduced semantic curriculum defect.** Generator SHA `39ac60c259165d082dfa437086cdd60af9a61ac3089c86e38f6bc23009da8187`; executed rule hash `fcbcb48853c9`.

The selected rule fills an inclusive orange span only when a row has exactly two orange endpoints **and every interior cell is zero**. A plausible shortcut ignores the clear-interior condition and fills every row with exactly two orange cells.

I sampled 600 ordinary draws per band using seeds `10000+i`, `sample_index=i`, `i=0..599`. Results:

| Band | Draws where rival fits | Draws containing a blocked two-endpoint row | Four-demo windows where rival survives |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| easy | 600/600 | 0/600 | 200/200 |
| medium | 600/600 | 0/600 | 200/200 |
| hard | 357/600 | 243/600 | 20/200 |

The 200 windows per band used inputs at indices `(start*7+j) % 600` for `start=0..199`, `j=0..3`. No ordinary draw in any band contained a row with three or more orange cells, so the “exactly two” branch is also not taught against that rival. Full probe: `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/probe.json`.

A documented `texture="span_already_filled"` override supplies a minimal lawful counterexample and passes `self_check`. Its active row is `[0,7,4,4,4,4,4,7,0,0]`. The canonical Racket rule leaves the row unchanged because the interior is blocked; the shortcut changes columns 1–7 to orange. Source/rule hashes, seed, input, actual output, rival output, and command are in `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/counterexample.json`; raw authority output is `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/racket.json`.

**Why this matters.** The generator can express the boundary case but the production sampler does not teach it in easy/medium and does not reliably teach it in hard. A four-example learner can therefore infer a wrong but perfectly fitting rule.

**Limit.** This probe tests one high-value rival and sampled windows, not every possible hypothesis or every production seed.

## 8922fefc96ff

**Reproduced semantic curriculum defect; audit target left unchanged.** Current generator SHA-256 is `39ac60c259165d082dfa437086cdd60af9a61ac3089c86e38f6bc23009da8187`. Canonical Racket `apply` executed rule hash `fcbcb48853c9`, matched the catalog, and recorded the same generator hash.

The intended rule fills between exactly two orange endpoints only when every interior cell is zero. A plausible shortcut is: **fill every row containing exactly two orange cells, without checking the interior**.

I independently sampled 100 five-pair lessons per band using seeds `0..99` and sample indices `0..4`, treating indices 0–3 as demonstrations and 4 as the query:

| Band | Pair draws with a blocked two-endpoint row | Rival survives all four demos | Survives demos and changes query |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| easy | 0/500 | 100/100 | 0/100 |
| medium | 0/500 | 100/100 | 0/100 |
| hard | 202/500 | 10/100 | 4/100 |

The retained ordinary witness is hard-band seed `22`, sample indices `0..4`. The rival matches all four canonical Racket demonstration outputs. Query row 5 has orange endpoints at columns 6 and 10 with interior `[2,0,0]`; the canonical rule leaves that row unchanged, while the rival paints through the color-2 blocker. The query passes `self_check`. Python canonical outputs match Racket on all five pairs.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/probe.py`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/report.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/episode-inputs.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/8922fefc96ff/rival-outputs.json`

A prior `evidence/review_index.json` report was used only as a lead. The current source hash, bounded census, seed-22 episode, validator result, and canonical Racket outputs were independently regenerated here.

**Suggested repair:** make occupied-interior two-endpoint rows ordinary in every band or guarantee at least one in the four demonstrations whenever a query may contain one; declare the unconditional-two-endpoint rival and enforce lesson identifiability. This finite census checks one named rival, not universal induction.
